newsitem.title: UK: British comedian reunited with joke books.
newsitem.headline: British comedian reunited with joke books.

text.p: Veteran British comedian Bob Monkhouse, the butt of as many jokes as he has made, was on Monday reunited with two joke books stolen last year.

Monkhouse, presenter of the National Lottery television show and a former joke-writer for Bob Hope, had offered a 20,000 pounds ($34,000) reward for the books which contained 500 pages of gags, plots and ideas.

The books, with jokes going back 25 years, were stolen in July 1995, prompting as much mock-relief among Britons as sympathy. Some columnists said they would pay double the reward for the books to remain lost.
Monkhouse originally offered a 10,000 pounds reward but doubled it when the books were not immediately returned.
Monkhouse's agent Peter Pritchard said he was handed the books at a meeting on Monday after he was contacted by a man asking for "a five figure sum". ($1=.5994 Pound)
